thesis: The diagnosis in the plank is right (Alaska offered a 50-year, 715.4-acre North Slope lease for a compute campus while having no state statute on data centers at all), but the instrument is broader than the New York model the platform text itself names, and because Chugach says the binding Railbelt constraint is GAS rather than a missing law, a no-threshold moratorium's real bite lands on the one place a facility can be built without competing with an Alaskan household for a kilowatt hour.
the_inversion: A moratorium with no size line does not stop what people are afraid of, it stops what happens to be permittable. The Railbelt grid-competing project is ALREADY blocked by gas supply. The North Slope campus makes its own power at the gas source. The net closes over the off-grid project and passes through the empty space where the Railbelt project would have been.
three_legs: The plank imported the standard itself: it says 'similar to New York State', and NY's pause is defined by exactly the three features Alaska's lacks (hyperscale-only, 12 months, GEIS off-ramp). Checking the platform's own citation is not the film's frame.
The candidate confirmed the breadth is a POSITION not an oversight: 'until we do, nothing should happen.' Not 'nothing at that scale'.
The cost of the missing threshold runs in the direction nobody expects, which makes it policy and not pedantry.
strongest_against: You are grading a campaign bullet point as if it were a bill. Nobody drafts a megawatt threshold into a platform plank. The substance is a 50-year commitment of 715.4 acres with no statute at all on who pays for the power, and JKT is the only candidate with any instrument on the table.
DATE_CAUTION: The primary DNR notice reads 2026-05-12 with comments closing 06-15; the safe set carries 05-19 extended to 07-17. PUT 'May 2026' ON SCREEN. Do NOT air a precise day until reconciled.
anchorage_point: Local government already built the narrower instrument the plank skipped: Anchorage Assembly 10-2, March 2026, AO 2026-27, first zoning definition of data centers, requiring utility documentation of sufficient capacity. A threshold-and-showing rule exists TODAY.
would_cut: The money-and-irony frame as a STRUCTURAL beat (the mandatory corrections consume the runtime the plank needs). Give it one line and move.
Any cut from Thomas's 'terrified' quote to Alaska grid material (misattribution, not a stylistic risk)
Every dollar size for Stak (20x discrepancy carries no information)
gigawatt / '30 percent more than peak demand' as anything but explicitly attributed reporting; prefer 715.4 acres and 50 years, which are PRIMARY
Outside-money framing (the unit error is the easiest way to make the whole piece wrong)
Gallup without 'in their local area' verbatim
any implication about the other 16 candidates' positions
the_two_questions: What size triggers it, and what ends it? Answerable questions to put to any of the 17 candidates.
